clue.text: A means of laying on tar

definitions.text: A means of laying on tar

parts.words: A means of laying on tar
parts.note: tar is a sailor, and laying on means flogging, so this is the whip once used on sailors rather than a tool for spreading pitch

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tar' tempts you to think of road surfacing, but in crosswords a tar is a sailor, and to lay on is to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: The naval lash with knotted cords was the standard instrument for flogging seamen.

clue.text: Cor! Maria is off to Brittany

indicators.note: something that is off has gone wrong, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise that Maria is leaving for the French coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is off' rearranges CORMARIA into the old Latin name.
explanation.definitionFit: Armorica was the ancient Roman name for the region of north-west France that includes Brittany.

clue.text: Oddly — and in a foreign manner

explanation.definitionFit: Done strangely or bizarrely, and also in the style of a distant alien land, the older sense of the word.

clue.text: Sin, lie — it can isolate one

indicators.note: read as 'the letters can become', telling us to rearrange the two words before it

explanation.surface: Sinning and lying are vices that can cut a person off from others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it can' signals that SINLIE can be rearranged into the rare verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To inisle is literally to make an island of something, so to cut it off and isolate it.

clue.text: Repeat the English church oratorio, first and last

indicators.note: the letter that both begins and ends the word oratorio is the one to take

explanation.surface: A choir is asked to perform the English church oratorio again from start to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first and last' picks O, which is both the opening and closing letter of 'oratorio', so only one O is used.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a sound reflected back and heard again, a repeat of the original.

clue.text: Leggings need openings made, we're told

indicators.note: a report heard rather than seen, so the word for openings is said aloud

parts.note: breaches are gaps or openings made in a wall or defence

explanation.surface: Trousers need some holes cut in them, someone reports.
explanation.definitionFit: Breeches are short trousers covering the legs to the knee, close to leggings.

clue.text: The vivacity of Italian music

explanation.definitionFit: Brio means liveliness or spirit, and it is the Italian musical term in the direction con brio, play with verve.

clue.text: Some gold lighters confiscated by religious Scotsman

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Golden cigarette lighters are seized from someone by a strict Scottish churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'confiscated by', which only links the hidden run to the definition; the definition itself is 'religious Scotsman'.
explanation.definitionFit: An Old Light was a member of a conservative faction in the eighteenth-century Scottish Presbyterian church.

clue.text: Soldier has bodily lost energy

indicators.note: the word for bodily has lost a letter, so one letter is taken away

parts.note: corporeal means bodily or physical
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A tired soldier has run out of physical strength.
explanation.definitionFit: A corporal is a non-commissioned army rank, so a soldier.

clue.text: A four-letter word constitutes obscenity

explanation.definitionFit: A four-letter word is a rude one, and smut is indecent or obscene talk; the word itself also happens to have four letters.

clue.text: Get hot and bothered

parts.note: becoming flustered is the opposite of keeping calm, so the phrase is read as losing one's composure or temperature

explanation.definitionFit: To lose your composure is to become agitated and flustered, an idiom meaning to get worked up.

clue.text: The EEC finds heath fair

parts.note: a common is an area of open land like a heath
a market or fair is a gathering for buying and selling

explanation.surface: The European Economic Community discovers open land and a fair.
explanation.definitionFit: The European Economic Community was popularly known in Britain by this name before it became the EU.

clue.text: They make advances in crossing rose with pine

indicators.note: crossing two plants as a gardener would mixes their letters into a new form

explanation.surface: Plant breeders make progress by crossbreeding roses with pine trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Pioneers are those who lead the way into new ground, making advances others follow.

clue.text: Taking a shot, an arm support is needed

explanation.definitionFit: A sling is a weapon for hurling stones at a target, and also a bandage hung from the neck to cradle an injured arm.

clue.text: Providing nests for pigeons?

parts.note: read literally as giving pigeons a home, though the word describes birds that find their way back

explanation.definitionFit: Homing pigeons return to their loft, and the word read playfully means supplying homes.

clue.text: Albi, or another holiday destination

indicators.note: another arrangement of the same letters is wanted, so the town's name is rearranged

explanation.surface: A French town is suggested as one possible place to go on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or another' rearranges ALBI, the French cathedral town.
explanation.definitionFit: Bali is an Indonesian island popular with tourists.

clue.text: In B & B as Arab enters — a famous criminal

indicators.note: one word goes into the other, so Arab is placed inside the two Bs

parts.note: the letters B and B as printed
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Arab guest checks into a bed and breakfast, and turns out to be a notorious villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters' puts ARAB between the two Bs before AS is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Barabbas was the robber released instead of Jesus in the Gospel story, a notorious lawbreaker.

clue.text: Despotic as the backward Roman was at tyre, almost

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written, spelt as the rubber wheel covering

indicators.note: the Roman's name is to be read from right to left

parts.note: Cinna was a Roman politician and conspirator against Caesar

explanation.surface: A tyrannical ruler is likened to a reactionary Roman who was in the city of Tyre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims TYRE to TYR; 'backward' turns CINNA into ANNIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyrannic is an old form of tyrannical, ruling cruelly and absolutely like a despot.

clue.text: Leave out first optional meal ingredient tested…

indicators.note: the opening letter of each of the following four words is taken

explanation.surface: A cook says to skip the first, optional ingredient of a dish that has been trialled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes the initials of 'optional meal ingredient tested'.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to skip or exclude it.

clue.text: Bar notices?

parts.note: bar suggests banning, but here it is a pub, and the notices are its hanging boards

explanation.definitionFit: Pubs traditionally hang painted boards outside showing their name.

clue.text: …it would be more unwise to use bacon

explanation.definitionFit: Rasher means more reckless, the comparative of rash, and it is also a thin slice of bacon.

clue.text: Go in — glam-rock at dusk!

indicators.note: to rock is to shake, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: An invitation to come inside for some glam rock music in the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'glam-rock' looks like the music style, but 'rock' shakes up GOINGLAM.
explanation.definitionFit: The gloaming is a Scottish and poetic word for twilight.

clue.text: Attractively mottled stone — hope it can be worked

indicators.note: worked suggests shaping material, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A stonemason hopes a pretty speckled rock can be carved.
explanation.definitionFit: Ophite is a green, spotted rock like serpentine, used decoratively.

clue.text: Child's of course taken by cockney woman kidnapper

parts.note: a baby is a young child, with the possessive kept
natch is slang short for naturally, meaning of course
a cockney drops the h, so her becomes 'er

explanation.surface: A London woman snatches someone's child, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class accent of East London, which drops initial H sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby snatcher is someone who abducts infants, a particular kind of abductor.

clue.text: Rolls barrel — spring back!

parts.note: B is an abbreviation for barrel in measures

indicators.note: the word for spring is turned to read from right to left

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: A barrel rolls along, and someone shouts to jump out of the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SPA into APS after the B.
explanation.definitionFit: Baps are soft bread rolls, a British term.

clue.text: Get back German sheep

indicators.note: the word get is written in reverse

explanation.surface: Retrieve a sheep of German breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tegg is a sheep in its second year, a dialect term.

clue.text: Say, in Kansas we keep beer in these!

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: KS is the postal abbreviation for Kansas
e.g. means for example, which is what say means here

explanation.surface: A Kansas brewer explains what they store their beer in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like the start of a sentence but stands for EG, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: Small barrels are what beer is stored in.

clue.text: Aiming at a snake, one coil visible

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
I is the Roman numeral for one
a ring is a loop or coil

explanation.surface: Someone takes aim at a snake whose single coil can be seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspiring means aiming or hoping to achieve something.

clue.text: Biggest outrage at the cricket match

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters of rage are rearranged

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: The largest scandal happened at a cricket game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outrage' reads as one word, but 'out' scrambles RAGE into GREA.
explanation.definitionFit: Greatest means largest or most important.
